title: Natural Hypertrophy: my lifting history
summary: NH recounts his training history: home calisthenics from age 15 at 120 lb, dumbbells for football and basketball, first gym and barbell at 20, self-programmed powerlifting from 21 to 22 (180 to 220 lb), then injuries and dissatisfaction with his physique led him to switch to bodybuilding about 2.5-3 years ago. He explains he started the channel to teach physique-focused natural lifters.

claims.claim: NH started lifting at 15 weighing 120 lb; he was so weak he couldn't do a single push-up and had to do them on his knees.
At the start he could only train about 10 minutes (knee push-ups, sit-ups, light pink dumbbell curls) but did it every day, eventually progressing to full push-ups and bodyweight squats.
With no gym or weights where he lived, he curled chairs and anything liftable; two years of bedroom calisthenics took him to about 140-150 lb by age 17.
At 17 he started high school football and bought adjustable dumbbells (about 50 lb total), doing lifts his coach suggested such as raises, curls and rows.
Early on he had no idea what he was doing and used the same weight for back rows as for biceps curls, even though the back is much stronger.
Dumbbell training alone took him to about 170-175 lb with decent definition by age 20.
From 19 he trained for basketball (weights, plyometrics, lots of swimming) purely for sport performance, not looks.
He first set foot in a gym at 20 after leaving his country for college, with five years of training behind him but never having touched a barbell, squatted or benched; he weighed about 180 lb.
For roughly his first year in a gym he did random workouts with no program before discovering powerlifting.

From 21 he trained powerlifting seriously on a self-made program of squat, bench, deadlift and their variations (paused bench, paused squat, front squat, paused/tempo/deficit deadlift), plus an arm day because he always liked training arms, but little else.
Between 20 and 22 he gained about 40 lb (180 to 220 lb) and got strong, but had mass only in chest, back and legs, with no lats or traps, bad shoulders, knee pain and back pain.

Unhappy with his look and injured, he stopped caring about numbers and moved to bodybuilding, realising he wanted to be big rather than lift a certain weight; he has done only bodybuilding for about 2.5-3 years.
Anyone whose goal is their physique is a bodybuilder, however they train, and NH created the channel because he now has the experience to teach such people.
